original_test_intent: Read firmware version from every expected LS10 NVSwitch using a vendor-approved query path and verify each physical switch against the correct platform manifest without altering switch firmware or fabric state.
original_method: Pin query utility and read-only semantics, inventory switch IDs/locations/fabric topology and expected count, collect complete per-switch version output through approved NVFlash or documented NVIDIA query, cross-correlate with HMC/BMC/topology evidence, compare each identity/version to manifest, verify fabric links/health and audit that no write/reset occurred.
manual_activity: NVSwitch/platform owner supplies expected switch topology/manifest and approves the exact read-only vendor query mode and owns discrepancy verdict.
required_inputs: Signed approved NVSwitch query utility/hash and semantics
Expected LS10 switch count, stable identity/location/topology map
Per-switch expected firmware manifest and revision
Protected evidence and no-write/no-reset audit policy
safety_requirements: Refuse unproven NVFlash target or any write/force/reset option
Capture complete output without grep/head truncation
Reconcile count and stable identity before version comparison
Stop on missing/duplicate/ambiguous switch or fabric health anomaly
Never update firmware in response to mismatch
agent_execution_scope: Run one approved read-only complete inventory
Compare every mapped switch and verify fabric health
Report without mutation or DUT verdict
engineer_actions: Approve query method and expected topology/manifest
Resolve missing, ambiguous or mismatched switch results

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Filtered/truncated nvidia-smi output may be corroboration but does not preserve source nvflash_mfg scope or complete all-switch results.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the vendor-approved read-only per-switch version query—source `./nvflash_mfg --v` only if documented for LS10, otherwise an explicitly approved equivalent—and preserve full output plus switch identities.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: All-LS10 scope, `--v` literal and five-minute timing remain; internal script must be pinned and reviewed before use.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Emit one record per physical NVSwitch with stable ID/location/fabric neighbors, query version, expected version and corroborating HMC/NVIDIA view, plus count and no-write audit.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Makes 'all correct' complete and topology-bound instead of relying on an untyped version list.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: GPU adapter VBIOS or NVFlash utility version cannot substitute for LS10 switch firmware.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Tool support differs by platform generation; only vendor documentation can establish whether nvflash_mfg addresses NVSwitches read-only.

project_override_considerations: Fabric owner defines expected switch count/topology and version compatibility across switch modules; absent devices require explicit disposition.
expected_evidence: Query tool signature/hash/version and read-only NVSwitch semantics
Expected switch count and stable ID/location/topology inventory
Complete raw per-switch output and corroborating NVIDIA/HMC/BMC inventory
Per-switch expected/observed firmware comparison and manifest revision
Fabric link/health and OS/BMC log delta plus no-write/reset audit

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Master consistently requires all LS10 NVSwitch firmware versions; query semantics are underdocumented but not internally contradictory.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Tool semantics, topology and manifest are provisionable; static review is complete.

review_improvement: Distinguishes NVSwitch firmware from GPU/utility versions and adds complete switch/topology reconciliation plus write containment.
independent_technical_reasoning: A fabric may remain partially operational when one switch is absent, so correct versions for returned devices do not prove all-switch coverage. Stable topology and expected count must precede version comparison. NVFlash is a firmware utility and its ability to address LS10 switches cannot be inferred from a similarly named GPU command; vendor-confirmed query-only semantics and a no-write/reset audit keep the readback safe.
